title: main-sync git-merge-main uses --no-ff so a diverged branch can sync, and its failure path is transactional

sha_binding.verified_source_note: Last commit on this branch touching a non-proof path (round-4 remediation). merge_sha is null pre-merge as the shared evidence contract requires (CEP-E7); it is bound to the real merge commit by post-merge-lane-close.yml.

verified_source_sha_history.superseded_reason: Round-1 head. Superseded by the P1 remediation commit: the --no-ff change made a conflicting merge reachable, and the wrapper failure path popped the lane-state autostash and released the merge mutex while MERGE_HEAD and unmerged index entries were still in the worktree.

Round-2 head. Superseded by the round-3 remediation commit: independent review found that abortInProgressSync collapsed an undeterminable probe result into 'the ref is absent', so a repository that could not answer took the 'nothing to abort' early return and the wrapper popped the autostash and released the mutex anyway -- the same fail-open class as the P1, one layer down; and that the caller-supplied onCommandFailure hook was called unguarded, so a throwing hook escaped runMergeWrapper with the lock held and no structured result.

Round-3 head. Superseded by the round-4 remediation commit: an independent reviewer demonstrated that the round-3 proof asserted the fail-closed message 'names the git command that actually ran' when commandVector rendered the bridged `git pull --ff-only origin main` instead -- a command that cannot leave MERGE_HEAD behind -- and that three further controls (the abort verb, the not-attempted stash pop, and the unmerged-paths term of the early return) were pinned by no test or mutant.

verdict.statement: git-merge-main built `git merge --ff-only origin/main`, which cannot merge a diverged branch by definition, so main-sync's recommended exit for divergence failed on exactly the condition it exists for -- leaving git-rebase-main, which rewrites history and invalidates every head-pinned governance artifact, as the only operable path. The command is now `git merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main`: it merges a genuinely diverged branch while preserving both sides' commit SHAs byte-for-byte, is deliberately not a bare `git merge` (which would fast-forward a merely-behind branch and make the verb's effect depend on divergence state), and is noninteractive. Permitting a non-fast-forward merge also permits a conflicting one, which exposed a second defect on the same path and was raised as a review P1: the wrapper popped its lane-state autostash and released the merge mutex while MERGE_HEAD and unmerged index entries were still present, stranding lane state in the stash and letting the next lane acquire a mutex over a half-merged worktree. The failure path is now transactional: abortInProgressSync aborts the in-progress merge/rebase and verifies the result before the stash is restored and before the lock is released, and a cleanup that cannot restore the pre-attempt state fails closed with the distinct merge_wrapper_cleanup_failed code, the mutex retained and the stash left intact. All five wrapper safety invariants are preserved; the mutex ordering is hardened, not weakened. Round 3 closed two fail-open residuals found by independent review: an undeterminable probe result (git exit 128) was being read as 'the ref is absent', which sent an unreadable repository down the 'nothing to abort' early return; and the caller-supplied onCommandFailure hook was called unguarded, so a throwing hook escaped runMergeWrapper with the lock held and no structured result. Both now force the fail-closed branch. The fail-closed recovery message also named `pnpm ops:merge-wrapper guard`, which only asserts the lock is held; it now names `pnpm ops:merge-lock release`. Round 4 corrected a FALSE claim that round 3's proof made and three controls that nothing pinned, all found by a second independent reviewer. The false claim: the fail-closed message was asserted to name the git command that actually ran, but commandVector was built from the bridged input, so it rendered `git pull --ff-only origin main` -- an invocation that cannot leave MERGE_HEAD behind -- and pointed the operator away from the residue. runMergeWrapper now takes a reportedCommand option: what is run is still `command`, what is reported is the caller's real vector. The three unpinned controls were the abort verb (hardcoding `merge` survived the whole suite; `git merge --abort` during a rebase exits 128 and the residue survives), the not-attempted autostash pop (test 49's assertions were satisfied by git's own refusal to pop into an unmerged index, not by the control), and the unmerged-paths term of the nothing-to-abort early return. Each is now pinned by a test and a mutant (M9-M12).

mutants.name: ['merge','--no-ff','--no-edit','origin/main'] -> ['merge','--ff-only','origin/main']
mutants.note: Killed behaviourally, not only by shape: 47-50 fail because the merge genuinely does not occur under --ff-only against a real diverged repository.

mutants.name: --no-edit removed
mutants.note: Killed by command-shape assertions ONLY. git merge --no-ff opens $GIT_EDITOR only when run from a terminal and the wrapper spawns git with piped stdio, so --no-edit cannot be made behaviourally load-bearing in this harness. It is the guarantee for tty callers; the shape assertion pins it.

mutants.name: onCommandFailure wiring removed from the sync path
mutants.note: Reproduces the reviewed P1 exactly: a conflicted merge again releases the mutex and attempts the autostash pop with MERGE_HEAD and unmerged entries still present.

mutants.name: abortInProgressSync failure return reports cleaned: true
mutants.note: Proves the fail-closed `cleaned` computation is load-bearing: a tree that could not be cleaned must never be reported clean.

mutants.name: the `if (cleanup && !cleanup.cleaned)` fail-closed branch removed, so the wrapper pops and releases anyway
mutants.note: Proves the fail-closed branch must exist at all.

mutants.name: an undeterminable probe treated as absence (`if (before.undetermined.length > 0)` -> `if (false)`)
mutants.note: Reproduces the reviewed round-2 P2 exactly: collapsing 'the probe could not answer' into 'the ref is absent' sends an undeterminable tree down the 'nothing to abort' early return, pops the autostash into a possibly-unmerged index and releases the mutex.

mutants.name: the try/catch around the onCommandFailure call removed, so a throwing hook escapes
mutants.note: Proves the hook boundary is guarded: without it a throwing caller-supplied hook exits runMergeWrapper with the lock held, the stash unpopped and no structured result.

mutants.name: the mutex released anyway inside the fail-closed branch, before returning
mutants.note: Proves the fail-closed branch must not release the mutex on its way out.

mutants.name: reportedCommand removed, so results name the bridged main-sync pull
mutants.note: Round 4. Reproduces the reviewed P2 exactly: the fail-closed result names `git pull --ff-only origin main`, a command that cannot leave MERGE_HEAD behind, pointing the operator away from the residue.

mutants.name: the abort verb hardcoded to 'merge' regardless of operation
mutants.note: Round 4. `git merge --abort` during a rebase exits 128 and the residue survives. It fails closed rather than open, but it converts automatic recovery into a manual-recovery incident for git-rebase-main. Survived the entire 52-test suite before test 53 existed.

mutants.name: a `git stash pop` attempted inside the fail-closed branch
mutants.note: Round 4. Test 49's `popped === false` and 'stash entry still listed' were satisfied by git's own refusal to pop into an unmerged index, so they passed under this mutant; the test now asserts the call was never issued.

mutants.name: `&& before.unmerged.length === 0` dropped from the nothing-to-abort early return
mutants.note: Round 4. Every real conflict leaves MERGE_HEAD too, so no test isolated the third term until test 54 masked both refs to ABSENT over a genuinely conflicted index.

scope_refusals: scripts/ops/merge-wrapper.ts was added to file_scope_lock for the P1 remediation only: the stash pop and the mutex release live there and nowhere else, and correcting the ordering elsewhere would have required re-acquiring a released lock, which is racy. One new optional option, one new result code, one guarded early return.
The dual-root sync-contract persistence defect in scripts/ops/codex-exec.ts was NOT bundled into this blocker fix.
The CPU/RAM scheduling contention observed during E2E runs was NOT bundled into this blocker fix.
No package.json, lockfile, tsconfig or build-config change. No workflow, branch-protection, proof-schema or bypass-flag change.
Four --ff-only occurrences belonging to main-sync's legitimate `git pull --ff-only origin main` were deliberately left unchanged.
known_gaps: A merge that conflicts still requires manual resolution by the operator. The wrapper now leaves the worktree exactly as it found it and reports actionably, but it does not resolve the conflict.

A --no-ff merge advances the branch head by one merge commit, which still moves the PR head SHA and therefore still invalidates head-pinned governance artifacts. This lane makes the sanctioned exit operable and SHA-preserving for existing commits; it does not eliminate re-authorization after a sync.
The cleanup-failure path deliberately leaves the mutex held. Recovery is manual and the message says so; there is no automatic lock expiry short of the lock TTL.
--no-edit is pinned by command-shape assertions only (see mutation M2); it cannot be made behaviourally load-bearing under piped stdio.

Rounds 2, 3 and 4 each installed the next defect, and two of the four found in round 4 were proof-integrity failures rather than product failures: a claim with no test behind it, and an assertion that could not fail. Recorded because the pattern is the finding.
